aspects.says: A class's runtime identity is its name plus its defining loader, so two loaders defining the same bytes give two distinct classes, while one loader defining a name twice is a LinkageError.
ClassNotFoundException is a checked failure of a dynamic lookup, while a failed static initializer gives ExceptionInInitializerError once and NoClassDefFoundError on every later use.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

aspects.says: The execution engine interprets bytecode, JIT-compiles hot code and runs the garbage collector.
aspects.reason: an overview the next two pages of this module (bytecode execution and JIT compilation) teach and practise in detail

aspects.says: The JVM initialises a class on exactly one thread, and other threads wait until it finishes.
aspects.reason: practised as the Holder idiom on the Singleton page (36-creational-patterns, 9.1.1)

aspects.says: Elastic Metaspace, CDS archives, heap-stored virtual thread stacks and string deduplication change the runtime areas' footprint.
Loading, linking and initialization are separate phases, and a class can be loaded without running its static initializers.
Each thread has its own Java stack, PC register and native method stack, while the heap and the method area are shared by all threads.
Metaspace replaced PermGen in Java 8: class metadata lives in native memory that grows on demand instead of a fixed-size part of the heap.
Generating classes without limit or leaking class loaders exhausts Metaspace, which -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize bounds.
aspects.reason: reproducing an OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace needs a JVM flag and minutes of class generation, which a practice test cannot set or afford

aspects.says: A custom class loader built with a null parent has the bootstrap loader as its parent, not the application loader.
new MyClass() loads and initialises the class if needed, allocates zeroed memory, sets the header and runs the constructor chain.
aspects.reason: the steps are internal to the JVM; the one observable part, that static initialization happens once and before first use, is graded in class-probe

aspects.says: A class loader asks its parent first and defines a class itself only when no parent can load it, so core classes always come from the bootstrap loader.
Unbounded recursion exhausts the thread stack with StackOverflowError, and -Xss sizes the stack.
aspects.reason: the depth at which the stack overflows depends on the stack size, the JIT and the frame layout, so no test can grade it deterministically
